Suspended holder, tabs B and C start in the same tick, both 45 s deadlines fired with a synchronous vi.advanceTimersByTime(45_000) (no microtask flush between them): B:NETWORK_ERROR, C:NETWORK_ERROR, server log [] (0 POSTs); releasing the holder afterwards still 0 POSTs, lock queue empty (aborted waiters removed), session r1 kept. new_findings.title: H-2 gap: reconcileBuyFlowOwner compares the NEW user id against getSession() (shared localStorage) before ef:lastuid (tab-local), so a user switch performed in ANOTHER tab (A logs out, B logs in there) is invisible: this tab already reads B from localStorage, keeps A's hold/queue/pay keys, and its next refresh overwrites ef:lastuid with B WITHOUT clearing - B resumes A's order (getActiveHold) in this tab
new_findings.evidence: Tab T: loginUser u-A (lastuid=u-A), buy-flow keys set, evenflow_hold_e1 = o-A. 'Other tab' replaces localStorage ef_token/ef_refresh/ef_user with u-B (what its logout()+loginUser does; its sessionStorage is its own). In T: getSession().user.id === 'u-B', getActiveHold('e1').orderId === 'o-A', ef:pay:o1 === 'A'. T then gets a 401 -> refresh for u-B -> setSession -> reconcile: prev = getSession().user.id = 'u-B' === next -> no clear; after it ef:lastuid === 'u-B' and all 6 keys still present, getActiveHold still o-A. Control: the same switch done in tab T itself clears all keys. D-F17's deferral reason ('other tabs lose access on next call via AUTH_REQUIRED') only holds for logout, not for logout-then-login-as-B, because the session store is shared localStorage.
new_findings.fix: In reconcileBuyFlowOwner prefer the tab-local record: `const prev = sessionStorage.getItem(K_LAST_UID) ?? getSession()?.user.id`. Additionally reconcile on reads, not only on setSession: in getSession() (or a `storage` listener for ef_user installed once per tab) compare the stored user id with ef:lastuid and call clearBuyFlowStorage() + update lastuid when they differ, so a tab that never refreshes also drops the previous user's keys.

new_findings.title: withRefreshLock only maps AbortError; any other rejection of navigator.locks.request (InvalidStateError when the document is not fully active / bfcache, SecurityError, NotSupportedError) escapes apiFetch as a raw DOMException (not an ApiError), no refresh is attempted and no fallback is taken; the proactive path swallows it but the 401 path rethrows it; a synchronous throw from locks.request additionally leaves the 45 s deadline timer dangling
new_findings.evidence: locks.request = () => Promise.reject(new DOMException('not fully active','InvalidStateError')): apiFetch('/v1/orders/o1') rejects with a DOMException named InvalidStateError (instanceof ApiError false), 0 POST /refresh, session r1 kept, timer delta 0. requestHold -> HoldClientError type 'AMBIGUOUS' (the generic catch), paymentFetch would map it to NETWORK_ERROR; waiting-room / organizer hooks that check `err instanceof ApiError` show the raw message. Proactive path (ef_expires_at in 10 s): error swallowed, request sent with the old token, then the 401 path throws the same DOMException. locks.request throwing synchronously (TypeError): rejection escapes and vi.getTimerCount() delta is +1 until the 45 s deadline fires (harmless: deadline.catch swallows; the abort just hits a controller nobody listens to).
new_findings.repro: it('non-abort lock rejection', async () => { vi.useFakeTimers(); Object.defineProperty(navigator,'locks',{value:{request:()=>Promise.reject(new DOMException('not fully active','InvalidStateError'))},configurable:true}); const {calls}=installFetch(c=>c.path==='/api/v1/auth/refresh'?json({}):problem(401,'/problems/token-expired')); seedSession('old','r1'); const tab=await newTab(); const err=await tab.api.apiFetch('/v1/orders/o1').then(()=>null,e=>e); expect(err).toBeInstanceOf(DOMException); expect(err.name).toBe('InvalidStateError'); expect(calls.filter(c=>c.path==='/api/v1/auth/refresh')).toHaveLength(0); const hold=await import('@/lib/hold-client'); expect(await hold.requestHold({eventId:'e1',ticketTypeId:'t1',quantity:1,queueToken:'q'}).then(()=>null,e=>e.type)).toBe('AMBIGUOUS'); });
new_findings.fix: In the .catch of `locked`, wrap every non-ApiError rejection as networkError() (session kept, no POST), e.g. `if (err instanceof ApiError) throw err; throw networkError();` (AbortError included). Build the `locked` promise inside the try block (or wrap locks.request in a `new Promise`/try) so a synchronous throw also reaches the finally that clears deadlineTimer.

new_findings.title: Design trade-off made explicit (H-1 comment 'KHONG timeout/abort POST'): a holder whose POST /refresh never answers (proxy black hole, no browser fetch timeout) keeps the Web Lock forever; its own request never settles and every authenticated request in every other tab fails with NETWORK_ERROR after 45 s, repeatedly, until that tab is closed - there is no retry, no abort and no user-visible way out short of closing the holder tab
new_findings.evidence: Refresh fetch returns a never-settling promise. Tab A's apiFetch is still pending at t = 143 s (settledA === false); tab B's three successive requests each end NETWORK_ERROR after 45 s (B0,B1,B2), exactly 1 POST /refresh total, session r1 kept. Not a regression (round 3 code had the same holder behaviour, and the 30 s steal was the bug); recorded because the simplification removed the only escape hatch and the spec/AC has no statement on it.
new_findings.repro: it('black hole', async () => { vi.useFakeTimers(); Object.defineProperty(navigator,'locks',{value:fakeLocks(),configurable:true}); const {calls}=installFetch(async c=>{ if(c.path==='/api/v1/auth/refresh') return new Promise(()=>{}); return problem(401,'/problems/token-expired'); }); seedSession('old','r1'); const tabA=await newTab(); const tabB=await newTab(); let settledA=false; tabA.api.apiFetch('/v1/orders/o1').then(()=>settledA=true,()=>settledA=true); await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(5); const out=[]; for (let i=0;i<3;i++){ const p=outcome('B'+i,tabB.api.apiFetch('/v1/orders/o2')); await vi.advanceTimersByTimeAsync(46_000); out.push(await p);} expect(out).toEqual(['B0:NETWORK_ERROR','B1:NETWORK_ERROR','B2:NETWORK_ERROR']); expect(settledA).toBe(false); expect(calls.filter(c=>c.path==='/api/v1/auth/refresh')).toHaveLength(1); });
new_findings.fix: Accept and document in spec.md (refresh has no client timeout by design; a hung identity call blocks all tabs until the holder tab closes), or add a long AbortSignal.timeout (e.g. 90-120 s, well above any realistic identity latency) to the refresh fetch and treat a timeout as AUTH_REQUIRED (clearSession, since r1 may already be consumed and must never be re-POSTed) so the user gets a 'sign in again' instead of an endless NETWORK_ERROR.

new_findings.title: H-3 residue: when addTier's RESPONSE is lost after the server created the tier (network error on a 201), the tier keeps its local id, is never matched to the server copy that the reload returns (matching is by id only), and every retry POSTs the same name again; per contracts.md:49 the server answers 422 'duplicate name', so the organizer is stuck on 'Hạng vé "...": duplicate name' until a full page reload (no duplicate tier, but no way to finish the save in the wizard)
new_findings.evidence: Mocked addTier #1 stores the tier on the server (srv-new-1) and then throws 'mất mạng'; getById after the failure returns the server copy. Second Lưu nháp: addTier called twice with name 'Hạng vé #2', the second call's tier does not carry id srv-new-1 (local id kept), push called only because the mock answered 201; with the contract's 422 the wizard would show the error again. EventWizard initialises `tiers` from initialEvent once (event-wizard.tsx:120), so the setEvent(await reload()) after the failure does not re-seed the tier list either.
new_findings.repro: it('lost response', async () => { const base=event(); mocks.update.mockResolvedValue(base); let onServer=null; mocks.addTier.mockImplementationOnce(async(_e,t)=>{ onServer={...t,id:'srv-new-1'}; throw new Error('mất mạng'); }).mockImplementation(async(_e,t)=>({...t,id:'srv-new-2'})); mocks.getById.mockImplementation(async()=>({...base,tiers:onServer?[...base.tiers,onServer]:base.tiers})); await renderPage(); await screen.findByText('Chỉnh sửa: Rock Fest'); next(); click('+ Thêm hạng vé'); next(); next(); click('Lưu nháp'); await screen.findByText(/mất mạng/); click('Lưu nháp'); await waitFor(()=>expect(mocks.push).toHaveBeenCalled()); expect(mocks.addTier.mock.calls.map(c=>c[1].name)).toEqual(['Hạng vé #2','Hạng vé #2']); expect(mocks.addTier.mock.calls[1][1]).not.toHaveProperty('id','srv-new-1'); });
new_findings.fix: In EditForm, after `current = await reload()`, also match unsaved tiers by trimmed name against current.tiers (names are unique per event per the 422 rule): if a server tier with the same name exists, treat it as the created tier (created.current.set(tier.id, serverTier) and compare quota) instead of POSTing; or map a 422 duplicate-name answer from addTier to that lookup.

new_findings.title: G-9 scope gap: only hold-client maps 403 /problems/forbidden; initiatePayment (and getOrderDetails/issueTickets) map a 403 forbidden to UNKNOWN 'Lỗi thanh toán HTTP 403', so a role/ownership problem during payment shows a generic system error instead of the new FORBIDDEN message; the approved TCR only covered hold-client, so this is a follow-up, not a defect of the approved change
new_findings.evidence: seedSession + fetch -> problem(403,'/problems/forbidden','role mismatch'): initiatePayment rejects with PaymentClientError type 'UNKNOWN', message matches /403/. hold-client control: 403 /problems/forbidden -> FORBIDDEN (status 403, no refresh, ef:hold:* key forgotten); 403 about:blank -> NOT_ADMITTED; 403 with empty body -> NOT_ADMITTED.
new_findings.repro: it('payment 403 forbidden', async () => { seedSession('acc','r1'); installFetch(()=>problem(403,'/problems/forbidden','role mismatch')); const e=await initiatePayment({orderId:'o1',holdId:'h1',method:'momo',buyerName:'a',buyerEmail:'a@b.co',buyerPhone:'0900000000',amount:100}).catch(x=>x); expect(e.type).toBe('UNKNOWN'); expect(e.message).toMatch(/403/); });
new_findings.fix: Add 'FORBIDDEN' to PaymentClientErrorType and map `response.status === 403 && type === '/problems/forbidden'` in initiatePayment/getOrderDetails/issueTickets; show checkout.forbidden in payment-view / order-result-view. Needs a TCR since payment contract tests pin the UNKNOWN mapping.

checked_no_finding: Holder 90 s + 3 waiters in 2 tabs: all waiters NETWORK_ERROR at 45 s (lock queue empty afterwards), session r1 kept; a user retry at 50 s while the holder is still in flight is QUEUED behind the lock (queued()===1), POSTs nothing, and at 90 s returns 200 with the rotated pair r2 (1 POST total). Holder 120 s: retry at 50 s times out again at 95 s (NETWORK_ERROR, no POST); retry at 125 s -> 200, 1 POST.

Logout in another tab while the holder's POST is in flight: logout POSTs r1 (server revokes), clearSession; the holder's late r2 is discarded (session null -> AUTH_REQUIRED), ef_refresh stays null (no resurrection). Same-tab logout during own refresh: AUTH_REQUIRED, session null. Logout while a waiter is still QUEUED: on grant doRefresh sees no session -> AUTH_REQUIRED, 0 POST.

Second user (u-2) logs in from tab B while tab A's refresh for u-1 is in flight: A's late r2 is dropped (storage holds u-2's pair, refreshToken differs -> returns u-2's access token), A's original request is retried with u-2's Bearer and completes 200 as u-2. Consistent with 'storage is the truth'; the server authorises the resource, no client-side issue beyond W-1.
AbortError rejections that are not ours (document unload etc.): NETWORK_ERROR, session kept, 0 POST.
No-Web-Locks fallback (two tabs): both POST r1 -> REUSE -> family revoked, all requests AUTH_REQUIRED (unchanged, deferred D-S-6); in-tab single-flight still 1 POST for concurrent requests.

Proactive vs reactive in the same tab (exp in 10 s, two concurrent requests): 1 POST (lastProactive guard + shared inflight). Proactive refresh answered 503: swallowed, request sent with the old token, 401 -> reactive POST (2 POSTs of r1, but the server had not rotated on 503 in this model; the backend caveat from round 3 stands). Reactive refresh in tab A racing a proactive refresh in tab B: 1 POST.

Deadline edge: lock handed over in the microtasks right before the 45 s macrotask -> granted wins, 1 POST, 200, no NETWORK_ERROR. Abandoned waiter granted later -> throws inside the callback (lock released immediately), never POSTs.

H-2: same id different role (buyer -> organizer) keeps keys (same person). Explicit logout removes ef:lastuid and keys; a later login finds prev null and keeps that tab's anonymous queue token (correct). clearSession() without buyFlow keeps lastuid (needed for G-4). Identity response with id '' -> nextUid '' guarded (no spurious clear, lastuid unchanged).

G-9 UI: FORBIDDEN banner shown, no BR-Q4/NOT_ADMITTED banner, no 'phòng chờ' link, no sign-in link, generic banner not duplicated, hold state back to idle (button enabled for retry), queue token kept. requestHold: forbidden -> FORBIDDEN with the ef:hold:* idempotency key forgotten (definitive 4xx).
Z-5 quota path: changing the quota of a tier created in a failed save, with BOTH reloads failing, still PUTs /tiers/srv-new-1 {new_quota} (created map keyed by server id).
suspicions_no_repro: Hidden-tab timer throttling (Chrome intensive throttling: 1 wake per minute after 5 min hidden) stretches the 45 s deadline of a hidden waiter; harmless (no POST) but a hidden tab's pending request may take minutes to fail. Not modelled.

Real Web Locks releases a lock when the holder's document is destroyed; the fetch of a closing tab is cancelled, but if the request already reached identity, r1 is consumed while storage still holds r1: the next tab to refresh POSTs r1 -> REUSE -> family revoked (forced re-login). Pre-existing, backend commit-before-respond; not reproducible in jsdom.
